The court held that the right "to dispossess the tenant was dependent upon a change in these conditions"; no contrary letting holding exists.

The hotel-use holding says the statute was "not applicable to plaintiff" and interference with his property was "unwarranted and unlawful"; the clean-hands ruling concerned his liquor certificate, not freedom to let rooms.

The operative decree was "enjoining the construction of an apartment house"; the observation that another neighbor kept boarders was evidence on waiver, not a contrary holding protecting this owner's letting.
The letting holding commands that the owners "shall not use the vacated apartment as a rental unit"; obtaining possession to cure the illegal unit does not affirm freedom to let it.

The court reversed the "erroneous legal conclusion that the appellants could not acquire a vested right in the occupancy provisions" and remanded to test that right; the municipality-interest footnote is not a contrary holding.

The court's single letting holding is that "the variance recommended by the Board and granted by the governing body is sustained" for the replacement hotel; residential zoning is background, not a contrary holding.

The operative holding protects the keeper from an unauthorized demand: 'the keeper of the boardinghouse is not bound to give the information required'; no contrary letting restriction was upheld against him.

Boarding the workmen is incidental to an attachment exemption dispute: 'the only question, therefore, is whether any of the goods attached were exempted from attachment as the law was when the writ was served.'

Two contrary liability holdings support mixed: the defendants 'were exonerated from liability for the money' if they complied with the safe-and-notice statute, but 'were liable for the other property' as absolute insurers.

The actual holding favors the innholder: because the persons might have been lodgers, 'he would not be guilty of any offence,' and the indictment was quashed; no contrary restriction on his letting was adjudged.

The checker is right because the holding enforces the property owner's control: permission for a manager 'did not authorize appellant to sublet to a tenant the entire premises and transfer the right of exclusive possession.'

The householder's board claim failed under the holding that 'the general burden was on the party setting up a contract, express or implied,' and the court overruled her exceptions; there is no contrary letting holding.
The checker is right: the court upheld abatement 'even to the extent of taking or destroying the property of an innocent owner,' a one-sided restriction on the hotel owner's use and letting.

The checker is right because the holding restricts this public landlord: 'a housing authority as here, does not possess the same freedom of action as a private landlord'; the private-landlord passage is a contrast, not a second holding.

The checker is right: for buildings erected solely to rent, the court held 'it would be a perversion of the spirit, letter and purpose of the constitution' to continue homestead protection; the protected garden was not rented.

The checker is right because the court enforced the private restriction, holding 'section 1566.5 has no retroactive application' and directing reinstatement of the injunction against the commercial lodging-and-care use.
